overview: A one-page list of papers summarizes four communications concerning a proposal by Mrs. William M. Hosken of the Hosken Trading Company to cooperate with Tokyo’s Hoshi Pharmaceutical Company in developing a cinchona plantation in Taiwan (then Formosa). In exchange for depositing funds in the Bank of Taiwan, Hosken would receive the exclusive agency outside Japan for Hoshi-produced quinine and hoped to finance the venture through the First Export-Import Bank with State Department support. The listed correspondence also records her introduction by Japanese consul Sawada, arrangements for her visit to Washington, and Eugene H. Dooman’s referral of her to Major Hall of the bank.

subfiles.about: The sheet inventories four papers concerning Mrs. Hosken’s proposed investment in a Formosan cinchona plantation and request for Export-Import Bank financing.
subfiles.summary: The list summarizes four communications dated February 22, February 25, February 27, and March 2 of an unspecified year. Japanese consul Sawada introduced Mrs. William M. Hosken to Eugene H. Dooman, after which arrangements were made for her Washington visit. Her proposal involved financing a cinchona plantation in cooperation with the Hoshi Pharmaceutical Company, depositing money in the Bank of Taiwan, and receiving exclusive rights outside Japan to sell Hoshi quinine. Dooman contacted Major Hall of the First Export-Import Bank and asked him to receive her, although the sheet does not record whether financing was granted.

interest: The sheet offers a compact map of a proposed trans-Pacific pharmaceutical enterprise linking American private capital, Japanese industry, colonial Taiwan, and U.S. government-backed export finance. It is particularly useful for tracing how personal introductions and State Department contacts facilitated commercial approaches to the First Export-Import Bank. The proposed exchange—investment in cinchona cultivation for an exclusive foreign quinine agency—also illuminates contemporary concerns about strategic drug supplies and the economic exploitation of Taiwan under Japanese rule.
